scope: Independent triage of selected findings in /tmp/clank-local-codeql/results.sarif; no repository edits.
result: No confirmed remotely exploitable production vulnerability among the assigned findings. Real conditional filesystem hardening gaps remain for locally writable backup/CLI paths and predictable benchmark report files.

evidence.sarif_snapshot: Read database/src.zip to map generated vendor findings to exact canonical source; current rebuilt vendor line numbers differ.
evidence.runtime_probe: matchRoutes with duplicate __proto__, constructor, prototype and toString keys preserved Object.prototype and produced only own query properties.
evidence.tests: node --test tests/dom.test.mjs tests/ssr.test.mjs: 44 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped; /tmp/clank-codeql-dom-triage.log
evidence.baseline: git diff shows no changes to recovery.ts, router.ts, dom.ts, ssr.ts or scripts/load files. CLI generation line750 is a new guard around a pre-existing path-based read, not a new remote entry point.

findings.production_reachability: Synth hydration is reachable, but the reported HTML interpretation is not. The server emits only its package-controlled frameworkVersion in boot state.
findings.reason: 248/252 write Text.data after a Text/nodeType3 check, so strings remain text. 455 inserts only an instanceof Node object; JSON.parse cannot construct DOM instances. 1060 consumes VNode.type only after the Symbol.for(clank.vnode) brand check; JSON cannot create symbol keys. SynthView uses frameworkVersion as a normal span child, never as a tag or dangerouslySetInnerHTML. serializeState escapes <, > and &, and SSR escapes primitive children. The intentional dangerouslySetInnerHTML API is not on the reported synth flow.
findings.action: No change required for these flows; generated files should map to canonical source in future scans.

findings.production_reachability: Public URL query names reach queryRecord by design, but cannot invoke prototype setters.
findings.reason: The first value uses Object.defineProperty to create an own writable data property, including __proto__. Subsequent assignment is reached only after Object.hasOwn found that property; repeats therefore modify the safe own property. Values are strings or string arrays. Runtime probe confirmed duplicate __proto__ leaves Object.getPrototypeOf(query)===Object.prototype.

findings.production_reachability: Functions are used by production backup read/verify/restore and new restore drills/PITR. Exploitation requires modifying or replacing entries/ancestors in the operator-selected backup repository during the read; an ordinary remote client or supported isolated Docker tenant has no such capability.
findings.reason: lstat is followed by open without O_NOFOLLOW/fstat identity binding. decryptFile then closes that handle and reopens the pathname for streaming, adding a second race. A local filesystem adversary could redirect reads or replace with a blocking special file. Platform repositories are projects/<id>/recovery (platform.ts13936), created/chmod0700; Docker runtimes mount the sibling data directory, not recovery. IDs are tightly validated, manifests use HMAC, ciphertext uses AES-GCM with authenticated manifest, and checksum/integrity validation precedes publication. Therefore the race is not evidence of arbitrary plaintext disclosure or forged-restore acceptance. Trusted process mode deliberately has host access and is outside tenant isolation.
findings.action: Defense in depth: pin repository ancestors, open once with O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK, fstat/bound reads and reuse that descriptor through streaming. Do not classify as remotely exploitable without an attacker-writable repository configuration.

findings.production_reachability: Only an explicit local CLI GitHub repository lookup, not a server endpoint.
findings.reason: The SARIF flow is package.json.version -> user-agent: clank-cli/<version>. It does not control the destination or transmit arbitrary file content. Destination is fixed https://api.github.com/repos/ plus URL-encoded repository segments, with redirects rejected, credentials omitted and bounded response/deadline.

findings.production_reachability: Installed local CLI commands only; requires an adversary concurrently changing the CLI user's project/fixture/workflow/config path. No HTTP handler invokes these functions.
findings.reason: 750 regeneration reads after lstat; 2189 preview --fixture reads after lstat and rechecks SQLite header/length afterward (so over-allocation can still precede rejection); 2894 workflow comparison reads after lstat; 3495 local JSON uses stat then readFile. Path replacement can defeat size/type/ancestor prechecks, redirect reads or block on a FIFO. Fixture content is uploaded only by the user-requested preview command to the configured authenticated platform. Config JSON is schema-validated; an attacker already able to modify credentials/config controls that local trust boundary. Regeneration now adds checks where baseline already used readFile.
findings.action: Future local hardening: descriptor-bound bounded reads plus pinned ancestors. Use private stable local workspaces/config directories; no confirmed new remote production path.

findings.production_reachability: Explicit local clank inspect artifact command.
findings.reason: The open uses O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK. fstat then checks regular file and dev/ino/size against lstat; reading is bounded to initial size+1 and a second fstat checks size/mtime/ctime. CodeQL reports the syntactic lstat/open pair without accounting for post-open identity and growth validation.
findings.action: No change required for the reported race.

findings.production_reachability: Opt-in development/load-test utilities, absent from the npm files allowlist and not imported by production entry points.
findings.reason: Default reports use predictable /tmp/clank-load-<kind>.json and /tmp/clank-load-reliability.json with writeFile truncation and no exclusive/no-follow open. On hosts permitting shared-temp symlink following, a local adversary can redirect report writes to another file writable by the benchmark user. Repeated checkpoints expose the same risk. This does not expose a production HTTP endpoint.
findings.action: Use an operator-owned --output directory now; prefer private mkdtemp output or exclusive descriptor-bound creation in a separate maintenance hardening change.

findings.production_reachability: Synthetic benchmark result aggregation only; not shipped production runtime.
findings.reason: run.mjs indexes local dictionaries by numeric HTTP status or fixed native error codes/fixed fallback strings. reliability.mjs uses Error.message only as a counter key; remote error bodies occur inside a prefixed assertion message, and values are arithmetic counters, not nested object assignments. Even a magic key cannot mutate Object.prototype through this single-level primitive write. Collisions can corrupt benchmark bookkeeping, not production object prototypes.
findings.action: Null-prototype counter dictionaries would be optional robustness hardening.

findings.production_reachability: Explicit synthetic-only staging service, requires CLANK_CAPACITY_ENABLED=synthetic-only and 256-bit token; all routes except health authenticate that token. Not an ordinary production server.
findings.reason: Logged value is native ClientRequest error.code or error.name, not response text, request URL, or arbitrary error.message. Current native error names/codes are fixed identifiers. No attacker-controlled newline path established. Fixture warns against co-location with customer data, requires dedicated capacity directory and shuts down after two hours.
findings.action: No production security fix required for this reported flow.

limitations: No filesystem race exploitation against production was attempted. Conditional local races are source-confirmed and not dismissed as scanner noise.
Canonical DOM source and exact extracted CodeQL snapshot were inspected; browser-based exploit reproduction was unnecessary for Text.data/instance guards, and existing DOM/SSR security tests passed.
Other assigned agents own notifications dynamic HTML and editor regex denial-of-service findings; they are intentionally excluded here.
